en.17:17: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who met him.
en.17:18: Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also were conversing with him. Some said, “What does this babbler want to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign deities,” because he preached Jesus and the resurrection.
en.17:19: They took hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “May we know what this new teaching is, which you are speaking about?
en.17:20: For you bring certain strange things to our ears. We want to know therefore what these things mean.”
en.17:21: Now all the Athenians and the strangers living there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell or to hear some new thing.
en.17:22: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said, “You men of Athens, I perceive that you are very religious in all things.
en.17:23: For as I passed along and observed the objects of your worship, I also found an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’ What therefore you worship in ignorance, I announce to you.
en.17:24: The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands.
en.17:25: He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath and all things.
en.17:26: He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings,
en.17:27: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.
en.17:28: ‘For in him we live, move, and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also his offspring.’
en.17:29: Being then the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Divine Nature is like gold, or silver, or stone, engraved by art and design of man.
en.17:30: The times of ignorance therefore God overlooked. But now he commands that all people everywhere should repent,
en.17:31: because he has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man whom he has ordained; of which he has given assurance to all men, in that he has raised him from the dead.”
en.17:32: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked; but others said, “We want to hear you again concerning this.”
en.17:33: Thus Paul went out from among them.
en.17:34: But certain men joined with him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
en.18:1: After these things Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth.
en.18:2: He found a certain Jew named Aquila, a man of Pontus by race, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome. He came to them,
en.18:3: and because he practiced the same trade, he lived with them and worked, for by trade they were tent makers.
en.18:4: He reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath and persuaded Jews and Greeks.
en.18:5: When Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.
en.18:6: When they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook out his clothing and said to them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am clean. From now on, I will go to the Gentiles!”
en.18:7: He departed there and went into the house of a certain man named Justus, one who worshiped God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.
en.18:8: Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his house. Many of the Corinthians, when they heard, believed and were baptized.
en.18:9: The Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision, “Don’t be afraid, but speak and don’t be silent;
en.18:10: for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.”
en.18:11: He lived there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
en.18:12: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,
en.18:13: saying, “This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.”
en.18:14: But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked crime, you Jews, it would be reasonable that I should bear with you;
en.18:15: but if they are questions about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves. For I don’t want to be a judge of these matters.”
en.18:16: So he drove them from the judgment seat.
en.18:17: Then all the Greeks seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. Gallio didn’t care about any of these things.
en.18:18: Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers, and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
en.18:19: He came to Ephesus, and he left them there; but he himself entered into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
en.18:20: When they asked him to stay with them a longer time, he declined;
en.18:21: but taking his leave of them, he said, “I must by all means keep this coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will return again to you if God wills.” Then he set sail from Ephesus.
en.18:22: When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.
en.18:23: Having spent some time there, he departed and went through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.
en.18:24: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures.
en.18:25: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, although he knew only the baptism of John.
en.18:26: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside, and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
en.18:27: When he had determined to pass over into Achaia, the brothers encouraged him; and wrote to the disciples to receive him. When he had come, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace;
en.18:28: for he powerfully refuted the Jews, publicly showing by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.
en.19:1: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus and found certain disciples.
en.19:2: He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “No, we haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
en.19:3: He said, “Into what then were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”
en.19:4: Paul said, “John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one who would come after him, that is, in Christ Jesus.”
en.19:5: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
en.19:6: When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them and they spoke with other languages and prophesied.
en.19:7: They were about twelve men in all.
en.19:8: He entered into the synagogue and spoke boldly for a period of three months, reasoning and persuading about the things concerning God’s Kingdom.
en.19:9: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.
en.19:10: This continued for two years, so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
en.19:11: God worked special miracles by the hands of Paul,
en.19:12: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried away from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.
en.19:13: But some of the itinerant Jews, exorcists, took on themselves to invoke over those who had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, “We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.”
en.19:14: There were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did this.
en.19:15: The evil spirit answered, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?”
en.19:16: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overpowered them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
en.19:17: This became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived at Ephesus. Fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
en.19:18: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing and declaring their deeds.
en.19:19: Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted their price, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.
en.19:20: So the word of the Lord was growing and becoming mighty.
en.19:21: Now after these things had ended, Paul determined in the Spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.”
en.19:22: Having sent into Macedonia two of those who served him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.
en.19:23: About that time there arose no small disturbance concerning the Way.
en.19:24: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no little business to the craftsmen,
en.19:25: whom he gathered together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.
en.19:26: You see and hear that not at Ephesus alone, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away many people, saying that they are no gods that are made with hands.
en.19:27: Not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.”
en.19:28: When they heard this they were filled with anger, and cried out, saying, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
en.19:29: The whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.
en.19:30: When Paul wanted to enter in to the people, the disciples didn’t allow him.
en.19:31: Certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent to him and begged him not to venture into the theater.
en.19:32: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another, for the assembly was in confusion. Most of them didn’t know why they had come together.
en.19:33: They brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. Alexander beckoned with his hand, and would have made a defense to the people.
en.19:34: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice for a time of about two hours cried out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
en.19:35: When the town clerk had quieted the multitude, he said, “You men of Ephesus, what man is there who doesn’t know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of the image which fell down from Zeus?
en.19:36: Seeing then that these things can’t be denied, you ought to be quiet and to do nothing rash.
en.19:37: For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of your goddess.
en.19:38: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a matter against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls. Let them press charges against one another.
en.19:39: But if you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.
en.19:40: For indeed we are in danger of being accused concerning today’s riot, there being no cause. Concerning it, we wouldn’t be able to give an account of this commotion.”
en.19:41: When he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
en.20:1: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
en.20:2: When he had gone through those parts and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.
en.20:3: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.
en.20:4: These accompanied him as far as Asia: Sopater of Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.
en.20:5: But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.
en.20:6: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.
en.20:7: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day; and continued his speech until midnight.
en.20:8: There were many lights in the upper room where we were gathered together.
en.20:9: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third floor and was taken up dead.
en.20:10: Paul went down and fell upon him, and embracing him said, “Don’t be troubled, for his life is in him.”
en.20:11: When he had gone up, had broken bread and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed.
en.20:12: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.
en.20:13: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.
en.20:14: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.
en.20:15: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.
en.20:16: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
en.20:17: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly.
en.20:18: When they had come to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,
en.20:19: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;
en.20:20: how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,
en.20:21: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus.
en.20:22: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;
en.20:23: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.
en.20:24: But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.
en.20:25: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.
en.20:26: Therefore I testify to you today that I am clean from the blood of all men,
en.20:27: for I didn’t shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.
en.20:28: Take heed, therefore, to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Lord and God which he purchased with his own blood.
en.20:29: For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
en.20:30: Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.
en.20:31: Therefore watch, remembering that for a period of three years I didn’t cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.
en.20:32: Now, brothers, I entrust you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
en.20:33: I coveted no one’s silver, gold, or clothing.
en.20:34: You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.
en.20:35: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”
en.20:36: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
en.20:37: They all wept freely, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,
en.20:38: sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
en.21:1: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
en.21:2: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
en.21:3: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria and landed at Tyre, for the ship was there to unload her cargo.
en.21:4: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
en.21:5: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.
en.21:6: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.
en.21:7: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.
en.21:8: On the next day, we who were Paul’s companions departed and came to Caesarea. We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.
en.21:9: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
en.21:10: As we stayed there some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
en.21:11: Coming to us and taking Paul’s belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘So the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”
en.21:12: When we heard these things, both we and the people of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.
en.21:13: Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
en.21:14: When he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, “The Lord’s will be done.”
en.21:15: After these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.
en.21:16: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would stay.
en.21:17: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.
en.21:18: The day following, Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.
en.21:19: When he had greeted them, he reported one by one the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.
en.21:20: They, when they heard it, glorified God. They said to him, “You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.
en.21:21: They have been informed about you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children and not to walk after the customs.
en.21:22: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.
en.21:23: Therefore do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow.
en.21:24: Take them and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses for them, that they may shave their heads. Then all will know that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.
en.21:25: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.”
en.21:26: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purified himself and went with them into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.
en.21:27: When the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,
en.21:28: crying out, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place. Moreover, he also brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place!”
en.21:29: For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
en.21:30: All the city was moved and the people ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Immediately the doors were shut.
en.21:31: As they were trying to kill him, news came up to the commanding officer of the regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
en.21:32: Immediately he took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them. They, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, stopped beating Paul.
en.21:33: Then the commanding officer came near, arrested him, commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done.
en.21:34: Some shouted one thing and some another, among the crowd. When he couldn’t find out the truth because of the noise, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.
en.21:35: When he came to the stairs, he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;
en.21:36: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”
en.21:37: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the commanding officer, “May I speak to you?” He said, “Do you know Greek?
en.21:38: Aren’t you then the Egyptian who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?”
en.21:39: But Paul said, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”
en.21:40: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people. When there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,
en.22:1: “Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.”
en.22:2: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,
en.22:3: “I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are today.
en.22:4: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women,
en.22:5: as also the high priest and all the council of the elders testify, from whom also I received letters to the brothers, and traveled to Damascus to bring them also who were there to Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.
en.22:6: “As I made my journey and came close to Damascus, about noon suddenly a great light shone around me from the sky.
en.22:7: I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’
en.22:8: I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said to me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.’
en.22:9: “Those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they didn’t understand the voice of him who spoke to me.
en.22:10: I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me, ‘Arise, and go into Damascus. There you will be told about all things which are appointed for you to do.’
en.22:11: When I couldn’t see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.
en.22:12: “One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus,
en.22:13: came to me, and standing by me said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ In that very hour I looked up at him.
en.22:14: He said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.
en.22:15: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
en.22:16: Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.’
en.22:17: “When I had returned to Jerusalem and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance
en.22:18: and saw him saying to me, ‘Hurry and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not receive testimony concerning me from you.’
en.22:19: I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue those who believed in you.
en.22:20: When the blood of Stephen, your witness, was shed, I also was standing by, consenting to his death, and guarding the cloaks of those who killed him.’
en.22:21: “He said to me, ‘Depart, for I will send you out far from here to the Gentiles.’ ”
en.22:22: They listened to him until he said that; then they lifted up their voice and said, “Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn’t fit to live!”
en.22:23: As they cried out, threw off their cloaks, and threw dust into the air,
en.22:24: the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted against him like that.
en.22:25: When they had tied him up with straps, Paul asked the centurion who stood by, “Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?”
en.22:26: When the centurion heard it, he went to the commanding officer and told him, “Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman!”
en.22:27: The commanding officer came and asked him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” He said, “Yes.”
en.22:28: The commanding officer answered, “I bought my citizenship for a great price.” Paul said, “But I was born a Roman.”
en.22:29: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, because he had bound him.
en.22:30: But on the next day, desiring to know the truth about why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from the bonds and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.
en.23:1: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”
en.23:2: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
en.23:3: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”
en.23:4: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”
en.23:5: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”
en.23:6: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”
en.23:7: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.
en.23:8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.
en.23:9: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”
en.23:10: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them and bring him into the barracks.
en.23:11: The following night, the Lord stood by him and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”
en.23:12: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.
en.23:13: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.
en.23:14: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, “We have bound ourselves under a great curse to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.
en.23:15: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”
en.23:16: But Paul’s sister’s son heard they were lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.
en.23:17: Paul summoned one of the centurions and said, “Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.”
en.23:18: So he took him and brought him to the commanding officer and said, “Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
en.23:19: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?”
en.23:20: He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.
en.23:21: Therefore don’t yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse to neither eat nor drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”
en.23:22: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”
en.23:23: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.”
en.23:24: He asked them to provide mounts, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.
en.23:25: He wrote a letter like this:
en.23:26: “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.
en.23:27: “This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them when I came with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.
en.23:28: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.
en.23:29: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.
en.23:30: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”
en.23:31: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
en.23:32: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.
en.23:33: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.
en.23:34: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,
en.23:35: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.
en.24:1: After five days, the high priest, Ananias, came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus. They informed the governor against Paul.
en.24:2: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that prosperity is coming to this nation by your foresight,
en.24:3: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
en.24:4: But that I don’t delay you, I entreat you to bear with us and hear a few words.
en.24:5: For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.
en.24:6: He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.
en.24:8: By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.”
en.24:9: The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.
en.24:10: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, “Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,
en.24:11: seeing that you can verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.
en.24:12: In the temple they didn’t find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the synagogues or in the city.
en.24:13: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.
en.24:14: But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;
en.24:15: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
en.24:16: In this I also practice always having a conscience void of offense toward God and men.
en.24:17: Now after some years, I came to bring gifts for the needy to my nation, and offerings;
en.24:18: amid which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, not with a mob, nor with turmoil.
en.24:19: They ought to have been here before you and to make accusation if they had anything against me.
en.24:20: Or else let these men themselves say what injustice they found in me when I stood before the council,
en.24:21: unless it is for this one thing that I cried standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today!’”
en.24:22: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, “When Lysias, the commanding officer, comes down, I will decide your case.”
en.24:23: He ordered the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody and should have some privileges, and not to forbid any of his friends to serve him or to visit him.
en.24:24: After some days, Felix came with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
en.24:25: As he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, “Go your way for this time, and when it is convenient for me, I will summon you.”
en.24:26: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often and talked with him.
en.24:27: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.
en.25:1: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
en.25:2: Then the high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him,
en.25:3: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem, plotting to kill him on the way.
en.25:4: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.
en.25:5: “Let them therefore”, he said, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”
en.25:6: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.
en.25:7: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove,
en.25:8: while he said in his defense, “Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.”
en.25:9: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and be judged by me there concerning these things?”
en.25:10: But Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.
en.25:11: For if I have done wrong and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
en.25:12: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”
en.25:13: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
en.25:14: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;
en.25:15: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, asking for a sentence against him.
en.25:16: I answered them that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction before the accused has met the accusers face to face and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.
en.25:17: When therefore they had come together here, I didn’t delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought.
en.25:18: When the accusers stood up, they brought no charges against him of such things as I supposed;
en.25:19: but had certain questions against him about their own religion and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
en.25:20: Being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.
en.25:21: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar.”
en.25:22: Agrippa said to Festus, “I also would like to hear the man myself.” “Tomorrow,” he said, “you shall hear him.”
en.25:23: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and they had entered into the place of hearing with the commanding officers and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.
en.25:24: Festus said, “King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
en.25:25: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor, I determined to send him,
en.25:26: of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination I may have something to write.
en.25:27: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.”
en.26:1: Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.
en.26:2: “I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you today concerning all the things the Jews accuse me of,
en.26:3: especially because you are expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.
en.26:4: “Indeed, all the Jews know my way of life from my youth up, which was from the beginning among my own nation and at Jerusalem;
en.26:5: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
en.26:6: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,
en.26:7: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!
en.26:8: Why is it judged incredible with you if God does raise the dead?
en.26:9: “I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
en.26:10: I also did this in Jerusalem. I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.
en.26:11: Punishing them often in all the synagogues, I tried to make them blaspheme. Being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
en.26:12: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,
en.26:13: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.
en.26:14: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
en.26:15: “I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ “He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
en.26:16: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen and of the things which I will reveal to you;
en.26:17: delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,
en.26:18: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’
en.26:19: “Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
en.26:20: but declared first to them of Damascus, at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
en.26:21: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.
en.26:22: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would happen,
en.26:23: how the Christ must suffer, and how, by the resurrection of the dead, he would be first to proclaim light both to these people and to the Gentiles.”
en.26:24: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!”
en.26:25: But he said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.
en.26:26: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.
en.26:27: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”
en.26:28: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”
en.26:29: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”
en.26:30: The king rose up with the governor and Bernice, and those who sat with them.
en.26:31: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”
en.26:32: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
en.27:1: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
en.27:2: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.
en.27:3: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.
en.27:4: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
en.27:5: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
en.27:6: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.
en.27:7: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
en.27:8: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
en.27:9: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them
en.27:10: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”
en.27:11: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
en.27:12: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking southwest and northwest.
en.27:13: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.
en.27:14: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.
en.27:15: When the ship was caught and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.
en.27:16: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.
en.27:17: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.
en.27:18: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.
en.27:19: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.
en.27:20: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.
en.27:21: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete and have gotten this injury and loss.
en.27:22: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
en.27:23: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,
en.27:24: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
en.27:25: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.
en.27:26: But we must run aground on a certain island.”
en.27:27: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.
en.27:28: They took soundings and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.
en.27:29: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.
en.27:30: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,
en.27:31: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”
en.27:32: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.
en.27:33: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.
en.27:34: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”
en.27:35: When he had said this and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; then he broke it and began to eat.
en.27:36: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.
en.27:37: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.
en.27:38: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.
en.27:39: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.
en.27:40: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
en.27:41: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.
en.27:42: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.
en.27:43: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;
en.27:44: and the rest should follow, some on planks and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.
en.28:1: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.
en.28:2: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the present rain and because of the cold.
en.28:3: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.
en.28:4: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.”
en.28:5: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.
en.28:6: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.
en.28:7: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us and courteously entertained us for three days.
en.28:8: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.
en.28:9: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came and were cured.
en.28:10: They also honored us with many honors; and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.
en.28:11: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose figurehead was “The Twin Brothers.”
en.28:12: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
en.28:13: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
en.28:14: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.
en.28:15: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
en.28:16: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
en.28:17: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
en.28:18: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.
en.28:19: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.
en.28:20: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”
en.28:21: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.
en.28:22: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”
en.28:23: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.
en.28:24: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.
en.28:25: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one message: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,
en.28:26: saying, ‘Go to this people and say, in hearing, you will hear, but will in no way understand. In seeing, you will see, but will in no way perceive.
en.28:27: For this people’s heart has grown callous. Their ears are dull of hearing. Their eyes they have closed. Lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, then I would heal them.’
en.28:28: “Be it known therefore to you that the salvation of God is sent to the nations, and they will listen.”
en.28:29: When he had said these words, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.
en.28:30: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house and received all who were coming to him,
en.28:31: preaching God’s Kingdom and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.

pl.1:1: Pierwsząm mowę uczynił, o Theophile! o wszystkiem, co począł Jezus czynić i uczyć,
pl.1:2: Aż do dnia, którego rozkazawszy Apostołom przez Ducha Świętego, które obrał, wzięt jest.
pl.1:3: Którym téż siebie samego po swéj męce stawił żywym w rozmaitych dowodziech, przez czterdzieści dni się im ukazując, i mówiąc o królestwie Bożem.
pl.1:4: A z nimi jedząc rozkazał im, aby nie odchodzili z Jeruzalem; ale czekali obietnice Ojcowskiéj, którąście (prawi) słyszeli przez usta moje.
pl.1:5: Albowiemci Jan chrzcił wodą, a wy będziecie chrzczeni Duchem Świętym po nie wielu tych duidni.
pl.1:6: A tak którzy się byli zeszli, pytali go, mówiąc: Panie! zali w tym czasie przywrócisz królestwo Izraelowi?
pl.1:7: I rzekł do nich: Nie wasza rzecz jest znać czasy i chwile, które Ojciec w swéj władzy położył.
pl.1:8: Ale oweźmiecie moc Ducha Świętego, który przyjdzie na was, i będziecie mi świadkami w Jeruzalem i we wszystkiéj Żydowskiéj ziemi i w Samaryi i aż na kraj ziemie.
pl.1:9: A to rzekłszy, gdy oni patrzali, podniesion jest, a obłok wziął go od oczu ich.
pl.1:10: A gdy pilnie patrzali za nim do nieba idącym, oto dwaj mężowie stanęli przy nich w białem odzieniu,
pl.1:11: Którzy téż rzekli: Mężowie Galilejscy! czemu stoicie patrząc w niebo? ten Jezus, który wzięt jest od was do nieba, tak przyjdzie, jakoście go widzieli idącego do nieba.
pl.1:12: Tedy się wrócili do Jeruzalem od góry, którą zowią Oliwną, która jest blizko Jeruzalem, mając drogę szabbatu.
pl.1:13: A gdy weszli, wstąpili do wieczernika, gdzie przebywali Piotr i Jan, Jakób i Andrzéj, Filip i Thomasz, Bartłomiéj i Mattheusz, Jakób Alpheuszów i Szymon Zelotes i Judas Jakóbów.
pl.1:14: Ci wszyscy trwali jednomyślnie na modlitwie z niewiastami i z Maryą, matką Jezusową, i z bracią jego.
pl.1:15: W one dni powstawszy Piotr w pośród braciéj, rzekł: (a był poczet osób wespółek jakoby sto dwadzieścia),
pl.1:16: Mężowie bracia, musiałoć się wypełnić Pismo, które opowiedział Duch Święty przez usta Dawidowe, o Judaszu, (który był wodzem tych, co poimali Jezusa,)
pl.1:17: Który był policzony z nami, i dostała mu się cząstka tego usługowania.
pl.1:18: A onci otrzymał rolą z zapłaty niesprawiedliwości, a obiesiwszy się, rozpukł się na poły, i wypłynęły wszystkie wnętrzności jego.
pl.1:19: I stało się jawno wszystkim mieszkającym w Jeruzalem, tak iż nazwano onę rolą ich językiem Haceldama, to jest, rola krwie.
pl.1:20: Albowiem napisano w księgach Psalmów: Niechaj będzie ich mieszkanie puste, a niech nie będzie, ktoby w niem mieszkał, a biskupstwo jego niech weźmie drugi.
pl.1:21: Potrzeba tedy z tych mężów którzy się z nami schodzili przez wszystek czas, którego Pan Jezus wchodził i wychodził między nami,
pl.1:22: Począwszy ode chrztu Janowego aż do tego dnia, w który jest wzięt od nas, aby jeden z nich był z nami świadkiem zmartwychwstania jego.
pl.1:23: I postanowili dwu. Józepha, którego zwano Barsabas, którego zwano Justem, i Macieja.
pl.1:24: A modląc się, mówili: Ty, Panie! który znasz serca wszystkich, okaż któregoś obrał z tych dwu jednego.
pl.1:25: Aby wziął miejsce usługowania tego i Apostolstwa, z którego wypadł Judasz, aby odszedł na miejsce swe.
pl.1:26: I dali im losy, i padł los na Macieja, i policzon jest z jedenaścią Apostołów.
pl.2:1: A gdy się spełniały dni Pięćdziesiątnice, byli wszyscy wespółek na temże miejscu.
pl.2:2: I stał się z prędka z nieba szum, jakoby przypadającego wiatru gwałtownego, i napełnił wszystek dom, gdzie siedzieli.
pl.2:3: I ukazały im się rozdzielone języki jakoby ognia, i usiadł na każdym z nich z osobna.
pl.2:4: I napełnieni byli wszyscy Ducha Świętego, i poczęli mówić rozmaitemi językami, jako im Duch Święty wymawiać dawał.
pl.2:5: A byli w Jeruzalem mieszkający Żydowie, mężowie nabożni ze wszego narodu, który jest pod niebem.
pl.2:6: A gdy się stał ten głos, zbieżało się mnóstwo, i strwożyło się na myśli, że każdy słyszał je swym językiem mówiące.
pl.2:7: A zdumiewali się wszyscy i dziwowali, mówiąc: Izali oto ci wszyscy, którzy mówią, nie są Galilejczycy?
pl.2:8: A jakóżeśmy słyszeli każdy z nas swój język, w którymechmy się urodzili?
pl.2:9: Parthowie i Medowie i Elamitowie i mieszkający w Mesopotamii, w Żydowskiéj ziemi i w Kapadocyi, w Poncie i w Azyi,
pl.2:10: W Frygii i w Pamphilii, w Egipcie i w stronach Libii, która jest podle Cyreny, i przychodniowie Rzymscy.
pl.2:11: Żydowie téż i nowo nawróceni, Kreteńczycy i Arabczycy: słyszeliśmy je mówiące języki naszemi wielmożne sprawy Boże.
pl.2:12: I zdumiewali się wszyscy i dziwowali, mówiąc jeden do drugiego: Co to ma być?
pl.2:13: A drudzy naśmiewając się, mówili: Że moszczu pełni są ci.
pl.2:14: A stanąwszy Piotr z jedenaścią, podniósł głos swój i mówił im: Mężowie Żydowscy i wszyscy, którzy mieszkacie w Jeruzalem, niech wam to jawno będzie, a przyjmijcie do uszu słowa moje.
pl.2:15: Albowiem nie są pijani ci, jako wy mniemacie, gdyż jest trzecia godzina na dzień.
pl.2:16: Ale to jest, co rzeczono jest przez proroka Joela:
pl.2:17: I będzie w ostateczne dni, (mówi Pan): Wyleję z Ducha mego na wszelkie ciało, a prorokować będą synowie wasi i córki wasze, a młodzieńcy wasi widzenia będą widzieć, a starcom waszym sny się śnić będą.
pl.2:18: A iście w one dni na sługi me i na służebnice moje wyleję z Ducha mego, i będą prorokować.
pl.2:19: I dam cuda na niebie wzgórę i znaki na ziemi nizko, krew i ogień i kurzawę dymu.
pl.2:20: Słońce się obróci w ciemności, a księżyc w krew, przedtem niż przyjdzie dzień Pański wielki i jawny.
pl.2:21: I będzie wszelki, którybykolwiek wzywał imienia Pańskiego, zbawion będzie.
pl.2:22: Mężowie Izraelscy! Słuchajcie słów tych: Jezusa Nazareńskiego, męża od Boga pochwalonego u was mocami i cudami i znakami, które czynił Bóg przezeń między wami, jako i wy wiecie:
pl.2:23: Tego naznaczoną radą i przejrzeniem Bożem wydanego, przez ręce bezbożników umęczywszy, zatraciliście.
pl.2:24: Którego Bóg wzbudził rozwiązawszy boleści piekła, jakóż była rzecz niepodobna, aby od niego miał być on zatrzyman.
pl.2:25: Albowiem Dawid o nim mówi: Upatrowałem zawżdy Pana przed sobą; bo mi jest po prawicy, abych nie był wzruszon.
pl.2:26: Dlategóż się rozweseliło serce moje, a rozradował się język mój: nadto i ciało moje odpocznie w nadziei.
pl.2:27: Albowiem nie zostawisz dusze mojéj w piekle, ani dasz świętemu twemu oglądać skażenia.
pl.2:28: Oznajmiłeś mi drogi żywota, i napełnisz mię radością z obliczem twojem.
pl.2:29: Mężowie bracia! niech się godzi bezpiecznie mówić do was o Patryarsze Dawidzie, że umarł i pogrzebion jest, i grób jego jest u nas aż do dnia dzisiejszego.
pl.2:30: Będąc tedy prorokiem, i wiedząc, że mu Bóg przysięgą przysiągł, iż z owocu biodry jego miał siedzieć na stolicy jego:
pl.2:31: Przeglądając powiedział o zmartwychwstaniu Chrystusowem, że ani zostawion jest w piekle, ani ciało jego ujrzało zepsowania.
pl.2:32: Tego Jezusa wzbudził Bóg, czego my wszyscy jesteśmy świadkowie.
pl.2:33: Prawicą tedy Bożą podwyższony, a obietnicę Ducha Świętego wziąwszy od Ojca, wylał tego, którego wy widzicie i słyszycie.
pl.2:34: Albowiem Dawid nie wstąpił do nieba, lecz sam powiada: Rzekł Pan Panu memu, siądź na prawicy mojéj,
pl.2:35: Aż położę nieprzyjacioły twe podnóżkiem nóg twoich.
pl.2:36: Niechaj tedy wie zapewne wszystek dom Izraelski, iż go i Panem i Chrystusem uczynił Bóg, tego Jezusa, któregoście wy ukrzyżowali.
pl.2:37: A usłyszawszy to, skruszeni są na sercu, i rzekli do Piotra i do innych Apostołów: Cóż mamy czynić, mężowie bracia?
pl.2:38: A Piotr do nich: Pokutę czyńcie (prawi), a niech ochrzczon będzie każdy z was w imię Jezusa Chrystusa, na odpuszczenie grzechów waszych, a weźmiecie dar Ducha Świętego.
pl.2:39: Albowiem wam jest obietnica i dziatkom waszym i wszystkim, którzy są daleko, którekolwiek przyzowie Pan, Bóg nasz.
pl.2:40: I wiele innych słów świadczył i napominał ich, mówiąc: Wyzwólcie się od tego narodu przewrótnego.
pl.2:41: Którzy tedy przyjęli mowę jego, ochrzczeni są: i przystało dnia onego jakoby trzy tysiące dusz.
pl.2:42: I trwali w nauce Apostolskiéj i w uczęstnictwie łamania chleba i w modlitwach.
pl.2:43: I przychodziła na każdą duszę bojaźń, wiele się téż dziwów i znaków przez Apostoły działo w Jeruzalem, i była wielka bojaźń we wszystkich.
pl.2:44: Wszyscy téż, którzy wierzyli, byli pospołu i wszystko mieli spólne.
pl.2:45: Osiadłości i majętności przedawali i podzielali nimi wszystkie, jako każdemu było potrzeba.
pl.2:46: Co dzień téż trwając jednomyślnie w kościele a łamiąc chleb po domiech, pożywali pokarmu z radością i w prostocie serdecznéj,
pl.2:47: Chwaląc Boga, i mając łaskę u wszego ludu. A Pan co dzień przymnażał do kupy, którzy mieli być zbawieni.
pl.3:1: A Piotr i Jan wstępowali do kościoła na godzinę modlitwy dziewiątą.
pl.3:2: A niektóry mąż, który był chromy z żywota matki swéj, był noszon, którego na każdy dzień kładziono u drzwi kościelnych, które zowią ozdobne, aby prosił jałmużny u tych, którzy do kościoła wchodzili.
pl.3:3: Ten, ujrzawszy Piotra i Jana poczynające wchodzić do kościoła, prosił, aby wziął jałmużnę.
pl.3:4: A patrząc pilnie nań Piotr z Janem, rzekł mu: Wejrzyj na nas!
pl.3:5: A on patrzył na nie, spodziewając się co wziąć od nich.
pl.3:6: A rzekł Piotr: Śrebra i złota nie mam; lecz co mam, to tobie dawam: W imię Jezusa Chrystusa Nazareńskiego wstań, a chódź!
pl.3:7: A ująwszy prawą rękę jego, podniósł go, i wnet były utwierdzone golenie jego i stopy.
pl.3:8: A wyskoczywszy, stanął i chodził i wszedł z nimi do kościoła, chodząc i wyskakując i chwaląc Boga.
pl.3:9: I widział go wszystek lud chodzącego i Boga chwalącego.
pl.3:10: A znali go, iż on był, który dla jałmużny siadał u drzwi ozdobnych kościelnych, i napełnieni byli zdumienia i zapamiętania z tego, co się mu wydarzyło.
pl.3:11: A gdy się trzymał się Piotra i Jana, przybiegł wszystek lud do nich do krużganku, który zowią Salomonowym, zdumiawszy się.
pl.3:12: A ujrzawszy Piotr, odpowiedział do ludu: Mężowie Izraelscy! co się temu dziwujecie? albo przecz się nam przypatrujecie, jakobychmy naszą mocą albo władzą uczynili, że ten chodzi?
pl.3:13: Bóg Abrahamów i Bóg Izaaków i Bóg Jakubów, Bóg ojców naszych, uwielbił Jezusa, Syna swego, któregoście wy wydali i zaprzaliście się przed Piłatem, gdyż jego zdanie było, aby był wypuszczon.
pl.3:14: A wyście się zaprzali Świętego i sprawiedliwego i prosiliście, aby wam darował męża mężobójcę.
pl.3:15: A zabiliście sprawcę żywota, którego Bóg wzbudził od umarłych, czego my świadkami jesteśmy.
pl.3:16: A w wierze imienia jego tego, którego wy widzicie i znacie, umocniło imię jego, i wiara, która przezeń jest, dała to zupełne zdrowie przed oczyma was wszystkich.
pl.3:17: A teraz, bracia! wiem, żeście z niewiadomości uczynili, jako i przełożeni wasi.
pl.3:18: A Bóg, co przez usta wszech proroków pierwéj opowiedział, iż Chrystus jego cierpieć miał, tak ziścił.
pl.3:19: A przetoż pokutujcie i nawróćcie się, aby były zgładzone grzechy wasze.
pl.3:20: Aby gdy przyjdą czasy ochłody od obliczności Pańskiéj, a posłałby tego, który jest opowiadany wam, Jezusa Chrystusa:
pl.3:21: Którego potrzeba, aby niebo przyjęło aż do czasów naprawienia wszech rzeczy, które opowiedział Bóg przez usta swych świętych od wieku proroków.
pl.3:22: Mojżeszci mówił: Iż proroka wzbudzi wam Pan, Bóg wasz, z braciéj waszéj, jako mię: onego słuchać będziecie wedle wszystkiego, cokolwiek wam mówić będzie.
pl.3:23: I stanie się, wszelka dusza, któraby nie słuchała proroka onego, będzie wykorzeniona z ludu.
pl.3:24: I wszyscy prorocy od Samuela i po nich, którzy mówili, opowiedzieli te dni.
pl.3:25: Wyście są syny prorockimi, i Testamentu, który postanowił Bóg z ojcy naszymi, mówiąc do Abrahama: I w nasieniu twojem błogosławione będą wszystkie narody ziemie.
pl.3:26: Wam najprzód Bóg wzbudziwszy Syna swego, posłał go, błogosławiącego wam, aby się nawrócił każdy od złości swéj.
pl.4:1: A gdy oni mówili do ludu, nadeszli kapłani i urząd kościelny i Saduceuszowie,
pl.4:2: Frasując się, iż uczyli lud, a opowiadali w Jezusie powstanie od umarłych.
pl.4:3: I poimali je i wsadzili je do więzienia do jutra; bo już był wieczór.
pl.4:4: A wiele tych, których byli słowo usłyszeli, uwierzyło, i była liczba mężów pięć tysięcy.
pl.4:5: I stało się nazajutrz, że się zebrali przełożeni ich i starsi i Doktorowie w Jeruzalem.
pl.4:6: I Annasz, najwyższy kapłan, i Kajphasz i Jan i Alexander, i ile ich jedno było z rodu kapłańskiego.
pl.4:7: A stawiwszy je w pośrodku, pytali: Którą mocą albo którem imieniem wyście to uczynili?
pl.4:8: Tedy Piotr napełniony Ducha Świętego, rzekł do nich: Książęta ludu i starsi słuchajcie:
pl.4:9: Jeźli my dziś sądzeni jesteśmy o dobrodziejstwo przeciw człowiekowi niemocnemu, przez coby ten był uzdrowiony,
pl.4:10: Niechże wam wszym jawno będzie i wszystkiemu ludowi Izraelskiemu, że przez imię Pana naszego Jezusa Chrystusa Nazareńskiego, któregoście wy ukrzyżowali, którego Bóg wzbudził od umarłych, przez tegoć ten stoi zdrowy przed wami.
pl.4:11: Ten jest kamień, który jest odrzucony od was budujących, który się stał na głowę węgła.
pl.4:12: I niemasz w żadnym innym zbawienia: albowiem nie jest pod niebem inne imię dane ludziom, w którembyśmy mieli być zbawieni.
pl.4:13: A widząc bezpieczność Piotrowę i Janowę, i porozumiawszy, iż byli ludzie bez nauki i prostacy, dziwowali się i poznali je, iż byli z Jezusem.
pl.4:14: Widząc téż człowieka z nimi stojącego, który był uzdrowion, nie mogli nic przeciwko mówić.
pl.4:15: A kazali im precz ustąpić z rady i namawiali się wespół,
pl.4:16: Mówiąc: Co uczynimy tym ludziom? gdyż jednak znak uczyniony jest przez nie, wiadomy wszystkim mieszkającym w Jeruzalem, rzecz jasna jest, a zaprzeć nie możemy.
pl.4:17: Ale iżby się więcéj nie rozsławiało między ludzie, zagroźmy im, aby więcéj w imię to żadnemu człowiekowi nie mówili.
pl.4:18: A wezwawszy ich, zakazali, aby koniecznie nie mówili ani uczyli w imię Jezusowe.
pl.4:19: Lecz Piotr i Jan odpowiedziawszy, rzekli do nich: Jeźliż jest sprawiedliwa przed oczyma Boskiemi, was raczéj niźli Boga słuchać, rozsądźcie.
pl.4:20: Bo nie możemy, cośmy widzieli i słyszeli nie mówić.
pl.4:21: A oni zagroziwszy, wypuścili je, nie najdując, jakoby je skarać, dla ludu, ponieważ wszyscy wysławiali to, co się było stało w tem, co się przydało.
pl.4:22: Bo było więcéj niż czterdzieści lat człowiekowi, na którym się stało to cudo ozdrowienia.
pl.4:23: Lecz gdy ich wypuszczono, przyszli do swych, i oznajmili im, cokolwiek do nich najwyżsi kapłani i starsi mówili.
pl.4:24: Którzy usłyszawszy, zgodnie podnieśli głos swój ku Bogu i mówili: Panie! tyś jest, któryś stworzył niebo i ziemię, morze i wszystko, co w nich jest,
pl.4:25: Któryś Duchem Świętym przez usta ojca naszego Dawida, sługi twego, powiedział: Czemu się narody wzburzyły, a ludzie próżne rzeczy rozmyślali?
pl.4:26: Stanęli królowie ziemscy, i książęta zeszli się w gromadę przeciw Panu i przeciw Chrystusowi jego?
pl.4:27: Albowiem się zgromadzili prawdziwie w mieście tem przeciw świętemu Synowi twemu Jezusowi, któregoś pomazał, Herod i Poncyusz Piłat, z pogany i z ludźmi Izraelskiemi,
pl.4:28: Aby uczynili, co ręka twa i rada twa postanowiły, aby się stało.
pl.4:29: A teraz, Panie! wejrzyj na pogróżki ich; a daj sługom twym ze wszystką bezpiecznością opowiadać słowo twoje,
pl.4:30: W tem, abyś ściągał rękę twoję na uzdrawiania, a żeby się znaki i cuda działy przez imię Świętego Syna twego Jezusa.
pl.4:31: A gdy się modlili, zatrzasnęło się miejsce, na którem byli zgromadzeni, i napełnieni są Ducha Ś. i mówili śmiele słowo Boże.
pl.4:32: A mnóstwa wierzących było serce jedno i dusza jedna, ani żaden z nich to, co miał, swem nazywał, ale było im wszystko spólne.
pl.4:33: A wielką mocą Apostołowie dawali świadectwo zmartwychwstania Jezusa Chrystusa, Pana naszego, i była wielka łaska nad nimi wszystkimi.
pl.4:34: Bo żadnego między nimi nie było niedostatecznego; gdyż którzykolwiek mieli role albo domy, przedawszy, przynosili zapłatę za ono, co przedawali.
pl.4:35: I kładli przed nogi Apostolskie. I rozdawano każdemu, ile komu było potrzeba.
pl.4:36: A Józeph, który nazwany był Barnabaszem od Apostołów, (co wyłożywszy jest, syn pocieszenia), Lewit, rodem z Cypru,
pl.4:37: Mając rolą, przedał ją, i przyniósł pieniądze i położył u nóg Apostolskich.
pl.5:1: A niektóry mąż imieniem Ananiasz z Saphirą, żoną swą, przedał rolą,
pl.5:2: I ujął z pieniędzy za rolą z wiadomością żony swéj, a przyniósłszy część niektórą, położył przed nogi Apostolskie.
pl.5:3: I rzekł Piotr: Ananiaszu! przeczże szatan skusił serce twe, iżbyś skłamał Duchowi Świętemu i ujął z zapłaty roléj?
pl.5:4: Azaż zostawiając nie tobie zostawało? a przedawszy nie w mocy twéj było? Czemuś tę rzecz do serca twego przypuścił? Nie skłamałeś ludziom, ale Bogu.
pl.5:5: A słysząc słowa te Ananiasz, padł i umarł. I przyszedł strach wielki na wszystkich, którzy tego słuchali.
pl.5:6: A wstawszy młodzieńcy, znieśli go na stronę, a wyniósłszy pogrzebli.
pl.5:7: I stało się, jakoby we trzy godziny, żona téż jego, nie wiedząc, co się było stało, weszła.
pl.5:8: I rzekł jéj Piotr: Powiedz mi, niewiasto! jeźliście za to przedali rolą? A ona rzekła: Iście, za to.
pl.5:9: A Piotr do niéj; Cóż to żeście się zmówili, abyście kusili Ducha Pańskiego? Oto nogi tych, którzy pogrzebli męża twego, u drzwi, i wyniosą cię.
pl.5:10: Natychmiast padła u nóg jego i skonała. A wszedłszy młodzieńcy, naleźli ją umarłą i wynieśli i pogrzebli podle męża jéj.
pl.5:11: I padł wielki strach na wszystek kościół, i na wszystkie, którzy to słyszeli.
pl.5:12: A przez ręce Apostolskie działo się wiele znaków i cudów między ludem. A byli wszyscy jednomyślnie w krużganku Salomonowym.
pl.5:13: A z innych żaden nie śmiał się do nich przyłączyć; ale je lud ich wysławiał.
pl.5:14: I więcéj przybywało mnóstwa wierzących w Panu, mężów i niewiast,
pl.5:15: Tak iż na ulicę wynaszali niemocne i kładli je na łożach i łóżkach, aby, gdy Piotr chodził, przynajmniéj cień jego zaćmił którego z nich: a byli uzdrowieni od niemocy swoich.
pl.5:16: Zbiegało się téż mnóstwo z blizkich miast do Jeruzalem, nosząc niemocne i nagabane od duchów nieczystych, którzy wszyscy byli uzdrowieni.
pl.5:17: A powstawszy najwyższy kapłan i wszyscy, którzy z nim byli, (to jest sekta Saduceuszów), napełnieni są zazdrością.
pl.5:18: I poimali Apostoły i wsadzili je do więzienia pospolitego.
pl.5:19: Lecz Aniół Pański w nocy otworzywszy drzwi ciemnice a wywiódłszy je, rzekł:
pl.5:20: Idźcież, a stanąwszy, powiadajcie ludowi w kościele wszystkie słowa żywota tego.
pl.5:21: Którzy usłyszawszy, weszli na świtaniu do kościoła i uczyli. A przyszedłszy najwyższy kapłan i którzy z nim byli, zwołali radę i wszystkie starsze synów Izraelskich i posłali do ciemnice, aby je przywiedziono.
pl.5:22: A gdy przyszli słudzy i otworzywszy ciemnicę, nie naleźli ich, wróciwszy się, oznajmili,
pl.5:23: Mówiąc: Ciemnicęśmy naleźli zamknioną ze wszystką pilnością i stróże stojące przede drzwiami; lecz otworzywszy, żadnegośmy w niéj nie naleźli.
pl.5:24: A gdy te słowa usłyszeli, urząd kościelny i przedniejsi kapłani wątpili o nich, coby było.
pl.5:25: A przyszedłszy ktoś, powiedział im: Iż oto mężowie, któreście wsadzili do więzienia, są w kościele stojąc i ucząc lud.
pl.5:26: Tedy poszedł urząd z służebnikami i przywiódł je bez gwałtu; bo się ludu bali, by ich nie ukamionował.
pl.5:27: A przywiódłszy je, postawili przed radą. I pytał ich najwyższy kapłan,
pl.5:28: Mówiąc: Rozkazując rozkazaliśmy, abyście w imię to nie uczyli; a oto napełniliście Jeruzalem nauką waszą i chcecie na nas przywieść krew człowieka tego.
pl.5:29: A odpowiadając Piotr i Apostołowie, rzekli: Więcéj trzeba słuchać Boga, aniż ludzi.
pl.5:30: Bóg ojców naszych wzbudził Jezusa, któregoście wy zabili, zawiesiwszy na drzewie.
pl.5:31: Tego Książęcia i Zbawiciela wywyższył Bóg prawicą swoją, aby dał pokutę Izraelowi i odpuszczenie grzechów.
pl.5:32: A myśmy są świadkowie tych słów i Duch Ś., którego dał Bóg wszystkim, którzy mu są posłuszni.
pl.5:33: To usłyszawszy, krajali się i myślili je zabić.
pl.5:34: Lecz wstawszy w radzie niektóry Pharyzeusz, imieniem Gamaliel, Doktor zakonny, w poważaniu u wszego ludu, rozkazał na mały czas ludziom wystąpić.
pl.5:35: I rzekł do nich: Mężowie Izraelscy! miejcie się na baczeniu z strony tych ludzi, cobyście mieli czynić.
pl.5:36: Albowiem przed temi dni powstał Theodas, powiadając się być czem, do którego przystała liczba mężów około czterech set, który zabit jest: a wszyscy, którzy mu wierzyli, rozproszeni są i wniwecz się obrócili.
pl.5:37: Potem powstał Judas Galilejczyk we dni popisu i uwiódł lud za sobą: i on zginął i wszyscy, i co ich kolwiek z nim przestawało, są rozproszeni.
pl.5:38: Przetóż i teraz powiadam wam: Odstąpcie od tych ludzi i zaniechajcie ich; albowiem jeźlić jest z ludzi ta rada albo sprawa, rozchwieje się.
pl.5:39: Lecz jeźli jest z Boga, nie będziecie mogli ich zepsować, byście snadź nie naleźli się z Bogiem walczyć. I usłuchali go.
pl.5:40: I wezwawszy Apostołów, ubiwszy je zakazali, aby zgoła nie mówili w imię Jezusowe, i puścili je.
pl.5:41: A oni szli od obliczności rady, radując się, iż się stali godnymi dla imienia Jezusowego zelżywość cierpieć.
pl.5:42: I nie przestawali każdy dzień w kościele i po domiech nauczać i opowiadać Jezusa Chrystusa.
pl.6:1: A we dni one, gdy rosła liczba uczniów, stało się szemranie Greków przeciw Żydom, iż w poługowaniuposługowaniu powszedniem bywały pogardzone wdowy ich.
pl.6:2: A dwanaście zezwawszy gromadę uczniów, rzekli: Nie jest słuszna, żebyśmy my opuścili słowo Boże, a stołom służyli.
pl.6:3: Upatrzcież tedy, bracia! z was siedmi mężów dobre świadectwo mających, pełnych Ducha Świętego i mądrości, którebyśmy przełożyli nad tą sprawą.
pl.6:4: A my modlitwy i usługowania słowa pilnować będziemy.
pl.6:5: I podobała się mowa przed wszystką gromadą. I obrali Szczepana, męża pełnego wiary i Ducha Ś., i Philipa i Prochora i Nikanora i Tymona i Parmena i Mikołaja, nowożydowina Antyocheńczyka.
pl.6:6: Te postawili przed oczyma Apostołów, a modliwszy się, włożyli na nie ręce.
pl.6:7: A słowo Pańskie rosło i mnożył się poczet uczniów bardzo w Jeruzalem, wielkie téż mnóstwo kapłanów posłuszne było wierze.
pl.6:8: A Szczepan pełen łaski i mocy czynił cuda i znaki wielkie między ludem.
pl.6:9: I powstali niektórzy z bóżnice, którą zowią Libertynów i Cyrenejczyków i Alexandryanów i tych, którzy byli z Cylicyi i z Azyi, gadając się z Szczepanem.
pl.6:10: I nie mogli się sprzeciwić mądrości i duchowi, który mówił.
pl.6:11: Tedy naprawili męże, którzyby mówili że go słyszeli mówiącego słowa bluźnierskie przeciw Mojżeszowi i Bogu.
pl.6:12: A tak wzruszyli lud i starsze i Doktory a zbieżawszy się, porwali go i przywiedli do rady.
pl.6:13: I postawili fałszywe świadki, którzy mówili. Ten człowiek nie przestawa mówić słów przeciw miejscu świętemu i zakonowi.
pl.6:14: Albowiemeśmy go słyszeli mówiącego: Iż Jezus Nazareński ten zburzy to miejsce i odmieni podania, które nam podał Mojżesz.
pl.6:15: A patrząc nań pilnie wszyscy, którzy siedzieli w radzie, widzieli oblicze jego jako oblicze Anielskie.
pl.7:1: I rzekł najwyższy kapłan: Jeźli się to tak ma?
pl.7:2: Który rzekł: Mężowie bracia i ojcowie! słuchajcie. Bóg chwały ukazał się ojcu naszemu Abrahamowi, gdy był w Mezopotamii, przed tem niż mieszkał w Charan.
pl.7:3: I rzekł do niego: Wynidź z ziemie twéj i z twojéj rodziny a idź do ziemie, którąć ukażę.
pl.7:4: Tedy wyszedł z ziemie Chaldejskiéj i mieszkał w Charan; a ztamtąd, gdy umarł ojciec jego, przeniósł go do téj ziemie, w której wy teraz mieszkacie.
pl.7:5: I nie dał mu w niéj dziedzictwa i na krok nogi, a obiecał mu ją dać w osiadłość i nasieniu jego po nim, gdy nie miał syna.
pl.7:6: I mówił mu Bóg: Że nasienie jego przychodniem będzie w cudzéj ziemi, i podbiją je w niewolą i źle się z nimi obchodzić będą przez cztery sta lat.
pl.7:7: A naród, któremu służyć będą, Ja sądzić będę, rzekł Pan; a potem wynidą i będą mi służyć na tem miejscu.
pl.7:8: I dał mu testament obrzezania: i tak zrodził Izaaka i obrzezał go dnia ósmego, a Izaak Jakóba, a Jakób dwanaście Patryarchów.
pl.7:9: A Patryarchowie nienawidząc Józepha, przedali do Egiptu, i był Bóg z nim.
pl.7:10: I wyrwał go ze wszystkich jego ucisków, a dał mu łaskę i mądrość przed oczyma Pharaona, króla Egipskiego, i postanowił go nad Egiptem i nad wszystkim domem swoim.
pl.7:11: I przyszedł głód na wszystek Egipt i Chanaan i wielkie uciśnienie, i nie najdowali żywności ojcowie nasi.
pl.7:12: A usłyszawszy Jakób, iż było zboże w Egipcie, posłał ojce nasze pierwszy raz.
pl.7:13: A za wtórym razem poznany jest Józeph od braciéj swojéj, i oznajmiony jest Pharaonowi naród jego.
pl.7:14: A Józeph posławszy, przyzwał ojca swego Jakóba, i wszystkiéj rodziny swéj w siedmdziesiąt i piąci duszach.
pl.7:15: I zstąpił Jakób do Egiptu, i umarł on i ojcowie nasi.
pl.7:16: I przeniesieni są do Sychem i położeni są w grobie, który kupił Abraham za summę śrebra u synów Hemora, syna Sychem.
pl.7:17: A gdy się przybliżył czas obietnice, którą był przysiągł Bóg Abrahamowi, rozrodził się lud i rozmnożył w Egipcie,
pl.7:18: Aż nastał inny król w Egipcie, który nie znał Józepha.
pl.7:19: Ten podszedłszy nasz naród, utrapił ojce nasze, żeby wyrzucali dziatki swe, aby nie żyły.
pl.7:20: Tegoż czasu narodził się Mojżesz i był przyjemny Bogu, który wychowany był trzy miesiące w domu ojca swego.
pl.7:21: A gdy był wurzuconywyrzucony, wzięła go córka Pharaonowa i wychowała go sobie za syna.
pl.7:22: I wyćwiczon był Mojżesz we wszelkiéj mądrości Egipskiéj: i był możnym w słowiech i w uczynkach swoich.
pl.7:23: A gdy mu się wypełnił czas czterdzieści lat, przyszło mu na myśl, aby nawiedził bracią swą, syny Izraelskie.
pl.7:24: A widząc niektórego ukrzywdzonego, obronił go i pomścił się krzywdy onego, który krzywdę cierpiał, zabiwszy Egiptczyka.
